summary: UK Part-FCL licences (issued by the CAA) are for life, but you need a valid rating and medical to use them. A PPL(A) needs a Class 1 or 2 medical, 45 hours (25 dual, 10 solo with a 150 nm cross-country and two full-stop landings away), nine exams within 18 months, and a skill test; minimum age 17, solo from 16. Class 2 lasts 60 months under 40, 24 months from 40, 12 months from 50. The SEP rating lasts 24 months: revalidate by a proficiency check in the last 3 months, or by 12 hours in the last 12 months (6 PIC, 12 take-offs and landings, 1 hour with an instructor). To carry passengers, do 3 take-offs, approaches and landings in 90 days (one at night for night). Cost sharing: up to 6 on board, pilot pays a share.
sections: Part-FCL and Part-MED
EASA licensing comes from the Aircrew Regulation (EU 1178/2011): Annex I = Part-FCL (licences), Annex IV = Part-MED (medicals).
After Brexit these became UK Part-FCL and Part-MED (assimilated law). The CAA issues UK licences; they are no longer EASA licences.
Aircraft that were "EASA aircraft" are now Part-21 aircraft. Exceptions: State aircraft (military, customs, police) and Annex I types (microlights, home-builds, historic), now non-Part-21.
Part-FCL licences are ICAO-compliant and non-expiring; using them depends on valid ratings and medicals. The LAPL is not ICAO-compliant.
Part-FCL terms
Category: aeroplane, helicopter, glider, balloon.
Class rating: a single-pilot aeroplane that needs no type rating (e.g. SEP land).
Type rating: a specific aircraft type.
Flight time: from when the aircraft first moves (own or external power) to take off until it comes to rest after the flight.
SPIC (student pilot-in-command): the instructor only observes.
Solo flight time: the student is the sole occupant.
Instrument time = instrument flight time (sole reference to instruments) + instrument ground time (in a synthetic trainer).
Revalidation: extends a rating that is still valid.
Renewal: restores one that has expired.
Skill test: for the issue of a licence or rating.
Proficiency check: to revalidate or renew a rating. (The book swaps these two definitions.)
Touring motor glider (TMG): fixed, non-retractable engine and propeller; can take off and climb on its own power.
Private pilot: may not be paid to fly (except instruction or examining).
Professional pilot: may be paid.
Night: in ICAO terms, end of evening civil twilight to start of morning civil twilight. In the UK, 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise.
Student pilots
Training starts without a licence under an instructor. A student may fly solo as PIC if:
– at least 16 years old
– holds a Class 1 or Class 2 medical and keeps to its limits (e.g. glasses)
– carries no one else
– is authorised and supervised by a flight instructor
Medicals (Part-MED)
A medical by an Authorised Medical Examiner (AME) is needed before applying for and while using a licence.
PPL(A): Class 2 (or Class 1).
LAPL: LAPL medical (or Class 1 or 2).
Professional pilots: Class 1.
Class 2 validity
Under 40: 60 months
40 to 49: 24 months
50 and over: 12 months
Valid for its full period even if you move into the next age group, but: issued before 40 → not valid after age 42; issued before 50 → not valid after age 51.
Renew up to 45 days before expiry without losing time (the new one runs from the old expiry). An initial medical runs from the date of the assessment.
LAPL medical: an AME or a GP; 60 months until 40 (not valid after 42), then 24 months.
Decrease in medical fitness
Don't fly if you know or suspect you are unfit. Get advice from an AME or AeMC without delay after:
– surgery or an invasive procedure
– regular use of medication
– significant injury or illness
– pregnancy
– admission to hospital or a medical clinic
– first needing corrective lenses
Rules of thumb: local anaesthetic 12 h, general anaesthetic 48 h, blood donation 24 h (bone marrow with a general: 48 h). Pregnancy: once assessed fit, flying up to the 26th week.
Pilot Medical Declaration (PMD): for some UK licences, flying G-registered aircraft in UK airspace, if you meet the DVLA Group 1 (car) standard.
The PPL(A)
Minimum age 17 (solo from 16). Train at an ATO or DTO. The CAA must be satisfied you are fit, knowledgeable and skilled.

Theory: 9 exams (Air Law, Operational Procedures, Navigation, Meteorology, Aircraft General Knowledge, Principles of Flight, Human Performance, Flight Performance and Planning, Communications), all within 18 months from the end of the month of the first pass. Credit then lasts 24 months for licence issue.
Also a radiotelephony practical, and a skill test with an oral.
Flying: at least 45 h, including 25 h dual and 10 h supervised solo, of which 5 h solo cross-country with one flight of at least 270 km (150 nm) and two full-stop landings at other aerodromes.
Pilots of another category (not balloons) may credit 10% of their PIC time, up to 10 h (not against the solo cross-country).
Not valid until signed in ink by the holder. Then valid for life.
A Part-FCL PPL(A) is also valid, with the same privileges, on non-Part-21 aircraft of the same class.
Privileges
PIC or co-pilot of aeroplanes or TMGs on non-commercial flights, with a valid class or type rating and a valid Class 1 or 2 medical.
No pay, except as an instructor or examiner for the LAPL(A)/PPL(A).
Cost sharing: allowed on private flights with up to 6 people on board, including the pilot, as long as everyone shares the direct costs, pilot included.
Glider towing or parachute dropping for pay is commercial, except at clubs whose aim is training or promoting aviation.
Passenger recency (FCL.060)
To carry passengers: 3 take-offs, approaches and landings in the preceding 90 days, in the same type or class (as sole manipulator of the controls).
At night: at least one of the three at night, unless you hold an IR.
FRTOL
A Flight Radiotelephony Operator's Licence is needed to use the radio (students have a dispensation). Pass the Communications exam before the licence; the practical can follow.
Ratings
SEP (land): almost all single-engine piston aeroplanes. Also MEP (land) and single-pilot (sea).
Differences training (logged, with an instructor): variable-pitch propeller, retractable gear, turbo/supercharging, pressurisation, tailwheel, single-lever power control, glass cockpits.
Revalidating the SEP class rating (valid 24 months)
Either a proficiency check with an examiner in the 3 months before expiry,

or, in the 12 months before expiry: 12 h in the class, including 6 h PIC, 12 take-offs and 12 landings, and 1 h refresher training with an FI or CRI (exempt if you passed another class or type proficiency check, skill test or assessment of competence).
An examiner or suitably qualified instructor then endorses the licence.
Lapsed: refresher training as required, then a proficiency check.
Other ratings
MEP: 70 h PIC first; ATO course; proficiency check in the 3 months before expiry.
Type ratings: complex single-pilot turbine aeroplanes and multi-pilot aeroplanes; valid 12 months.
Night rating: to use the licence in VMC at night.

IR(R) / IMC rating (UK only): 25 h after PPL, 10 h PIC (5 h cross-country), 15 h instrument training (10 h sole reference), written exam and test. IFR anywhere except Class A, and not to take off or land with flight visibility below cloud under 1,500 m. Valid 25 months.
IR(A): IFR down to a decision height of 200 ft (60 m).
Also aerobatic, sailplane towing, banner towing and mountain ratings; FI certificates (an FI(R) may not authorise first solos).
Other licences

LAPL(A): leisure, no pay; age 17; aircraft MTOW 2,000 kg or less, at most 3 passengers (4 on board); passengers only after 10 h as PIC after issue. Training 30 h minimum (book: 15 h dual, 6 h solo, 80 nm cross-country). Recency: 12 h PIC in 24 months with 12 take-offs and landings and 1 h with an instructor.
UK (ANO) PPL: Schedule 8; a UK PPL(A) may not fly out of sight of the surface without an IMC rating or IR.
NPPL(A) SSEA/SLMG (administered by the LAA): UK airspace only, day VFR, max 4 on board, MTOW 2,000 kg, 140 kt cruise limit; training 22 h dual and 10 h solo; ratings valid 24 months.
Microlights: two seats at most, Permit to Fly, weight and stall-speed limits (the book's mass limits are out of date; check the CAA's current definition).
Also: PPL(H), PPL(As), SPL (sailplanes), BPL (balloons), UK PPL(G) (gyroplanes, not ICAO).
Personal flying logbook

Kept by qualified pilots and anyone training for a licence: name and address, licence details, and for each flight the date, places, times, aircraft type and registration, capacity (dual, PIC), night/instrument, and any tests.
Damaging, altering or falsifying logbook entries is an offence (it amounts to forgery).
Produce it to an authorised person within a reasonable time, for up to 2 years after the last entry.

sum.Part-FCL and Part-MED: UK Part-FCL and Part-MED, issued by the CAA, cover Part-21 aircraft; licences are for life.
sum.Part-FCL terms: Key definitions: class and type ratings, flight time, revalidation versus renewal, skill test versus proficiency check.
sum.Student pilots: Solo from 16 with a Class 1 or 2 medical, nobody else on board, authorised by an instructor.
sum.Medicals (Part-MED): PPL needs Class 2 (or Class 1); LAPL can use a LAPL medical.
sum.Class 2 validity: 60 months under 40, 24 months from 40, 12 months from 50; renew up to 45 days early.
sum.Decrease in medical fitness: Unfit or in doubt: don't fly, see your AME. Local anaesthetic 12 h, general 48 h, blood 24 h.
sum.The PPL(A): Age 17; 45 h with 25 dual and 10 solo; nine exams in 18 months; signed in ink and valid for life.
sum.Privileges: Non-commercial PIC or co-pilot; cost sharing with up to 6 on board, pilot pays a share.
sum.Passenger recency (FCL.060): 3 take-offs, approaches and landings in 90 days; one at night for night passengers.
sum.FRTOL: You need a radio licence to use the aircraft radio.
sum.Ratings: Class ratings like SEP (land); differences training for things like retractable gear, VP props and tailwheels.
sum.Revalidating the SEP class rating (valid: Proficiency check in the last 3 months, or 12 h in the last 12 months with 6 PIC, 12 landings and 1 h with an instructor.
sum.Other ratings: Night, IR(R)/IMC (UK only, 25 months), IR, type ratings (12 months) and instructor certificates.
sum.Other licences: LAPL: 2,000 kg, 3 passengers, Europe. NPPL: UK day VFR, 4 on board. Plus PPL(H), SPL, BPL.
sum.Personal flying logbook: Record every flight; falsifying it is an offence; produce it for 2 years after the last entry.

cards.q: Minimum age for a PPL(A)? For solo?

cards.a: 60 months (but not beyond age 42 if issued before 40).

cards.q: How early can you renew a medical without losing time?
Who do you see after a significant illness or injury?
cards.a: Your AME (or an AeMC), before flying again.

cards.q: Rule of thumb after a local / general anaesthetic?

cards.a: 45 h, including 25 h dual and 10 h supervised solo.
At least 150 nm (270 km) solo with two full-stop landings at other aerodromes.

cards.q: How long do you have to pass the nine exams?
cards.a: 18 months from the end of the month of the first pass.
3 take-offs, approaches and landings in the preceding 90 days (one at night for night passengers).
Private flight, up to 6 people on board including the pilot, and the pilot pays a share.
In the 12 months before expiry: 12 h, 6 h PIC, 12 take-offs and 12 landings, 1 h with an FI or CRI.
A proficiency check with an examiner in the 3 months before expiry.
MTOW 2,000 kg or less and no more than 3 passengers.
Revalidation extends a valid rating; renewal restores an expired one.

cards.q: How long must you be able to produce your logbook?
cards.a: Up to 2 years after the last entry.

quiz.q: A pilot who is 38 passes a Class 2 medical. It is valid for:
quiz.why: Under 40 it's 60 months, but one issued before 40 lapses at 42. Lapsing at exactly 40 is the trap.

quiz.q: A Class 2 medical issued to a 52-year-old is valid for:
Before carrying passengers, a PPL(A) holder must have made, in the same class or type:
o: 3 take-offs, approaches and landings in the preceding 90 days
3 take-offs and landings in the preceding 60 days
5 take-offs and landings in the preceding 90 days
3 take-offs, approaches and landings in the preceding calendar month
quiz.why: Three in 90 days, as sole manipulator of the controls. For night passengers one must be at night.

quiz.q: Which is a valid way to revalidate an SEP class rating?
o: 12 h in the 12 months before expiry, with 6 h PIC, 12 take-offs and landings and 1 h with an instructor
12 h in the 12 months before expiry, with 6 take-offs and landings and 2 h with an instructor
A proficiency check with an examiner in the 12 months before expiry
6 h PIC in the 6 months before expiry
quiz.why: Experience route: 12 h, 6 PIC, 12 and 12, 1 h refresher. The proficiency check must fall in the last 3 months, not 12.

quiz.q: Cost sharing on a private flight is allowed when:
o: There are no more than 6 people on board and the pilot pays a share
There are no more than 6 people on board and the passengers pay everything
There are no more than 4 people on board and the pilot pays a share
The pilot holds an instructor rating
quiz.why: Up to 6 on board, and direct costs are shared by everyone including the pilot.

quiz.q: A student pilot may fly solo without a licence if they are at least:
o: 16, hold a Class 1 or 2 medical and are authorised and supervised by an instructor
16 and hold a LAPL medical, with one passenger
16, with written permission from the CAA
quiz.why: 16, a Class 1 or 2 medical, no one else on board, and an instructor's authorisation and supervision.

quiz.q: After a dental local anaesthetic, a pilot should not fly for at least:
quiz.why: 12 hours for a local; 48 hours for a general anaesthetic.

quiz.q: A pilot is admitted to hospital overnight. What must they do before flying again?
o: Seek advice from their AME or an AeMC
Get a note from their GP
quiz.why: Hospital admission is one of the triggers; the AME or AeMC decides fitness.

quiz.q: A LAPL(A) holder could act as PIC of an aeroplane with:
quiz.why: LAPL(A): 2,000 kg or less and no more than 3 passengers, so 4 seats at most.

quiz.q: Under Part-FCL, a 'proficiency check' is used to:
o: Issue a licence for the first time
Test a student before first solo
quiz.why: A skill test is for issue; a proficiency check revalidates or renews. The book's glossary has these the wrong way round.
